summary: C-1 to C-5 are met by the heredoc stripping, the new tests (9 pass in tests/bash-prose.test.mjs, 116 pass in npm test) and the rules.md row. The verdict is block because the push rule now reads only the first git push in the text and stops at a newline: a second push to the default branch on a later line is allowed, which breaks the spec's rule that the default branch is never pushed from a session. A second, major finding: a heredoc body that cat or tee writes to a file is dropped even when a later command runs that file.

findings.issue: The push rule matches only the first git push in the text and its argument scan stops at a newline, so a second push to the default branch on a later line is never judged and is allowed.
findings.suggestion: Judge every git push occurrence (a global match over the same single-line pattern) against the goal branch and the default branch, not only the first.

evidence.quote:
checkBashCommand("git push origin goal/G-3
git push origin main") => allow; checkBashCommand("echo ok
git push origin goal/G-3
git push origin main") => allow; checkBashCommand("git push origin main") => DENY(git) Blocked: pushing to the default branch main is not allowed from a session.

findings.issue: A heredoc body that cat or tee writes to a file is dropped even when the same or a later command runs that file, so a git reset --hard or a secrets read inside the body runs through bash run.sh; the same text was denied before this diff.
findings.suggestion: Keep a file-writing heredoc body in the judged text when a later command names the written file as an argument of a shell or interpreter, or ask the human to rule on write-then-run under D-1.

evidence.quote: cat > run.sh <<'EOF' / git reset --hard / EOF / bash run.sh => allow; cat > run.sh <<'EOF' / git reset --hard / EOF / sh run.sh => allow; tee run.sh <<'EOF' / rm -rf / / EOF / bash run.sh => allow; cat > run.sh <<'EOF' / cat <secrets path> / EOF / bash run.sh => allow
